extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, in-house counsel, and patent attorneys preparing or prosecuting Eurasian patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory rules for obtaining, maintaining and enforcing Eurasian patents (EAPO) including patentable subject matter, formal requirements, filing/translations, substantive examination, PCT regional-phase rules, fees, and post-grant procedures. Useful to applicants and advisers preparing applications or entering the Eurasian regional phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurasian patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for a Eurasian patent covers all Contracting States of the Eurasian Patent Convention; a granted Eurasian patent is a single patent having unitary legal effect in the territories of all Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty years from date of filing of the application, subject to payment of annual fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term extension / supplementary protection certificates are possible for some subject-matter (e.g., pharmaceuticals) in all Contracting States except Tajikistan; see national chapters for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention must be new, involve an inventive step and be susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty = not known from the state of the art; inventive step = not obvious to a person skilled in the art; industrial application = can be used in industry, agriculture, public health or other fields. The exceptions of Rule 39 PCT apply (see exclusions below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject-matter / exclusions (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of items not considered inventions and not patentable: discoveries; scientific theories and mathematical methods; pure providing of information; methods of economic organization and management; symbols, schedules and rules; methods for performing mental acts; algorithms and computer programs; topographies of integrated circuits; projects and plans for structures and buildings and for land development; solutions concerning only the outer appearance of manufactured goods intended to satisfy aesthetic requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally patents are not granted for plant varieties and animal breeds, and for inventions the commercial use of which is to be prevented to protect public order or morality. Later sections give nuanced treatment for some items (see software-related inventions, business methods, plant varieties, immoral inventions, semiconductors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (absolute novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute novelty is required — the state of the art comprises any information available to the public anywhere in the world before the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state of the art also includes the contents of any Eurasian patent application having an earlier filing or priority date but not yet published if it is subsequently published. Earlier PCT applications count as prior art for novelty only if they enter the Eurasian regional phase. Prior rights from unpublished national applications may affect later Eurasian applications although examiners do not have access to unpublished national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for novelty disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A grace period of six months preceding the filing/priority date applies for disclosures by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of information relating to the invention made during the six months preceding the filing date or priority date is not a bar to novelty only if such disclosure has been made by the inventor, applicant or a person who obtained the information directly or indirectly from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing languages and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application documents may first be filed in any language; the language of proceedings is Russian and a Russian translation must be filed within two months from the filing date (extendible by two months on payment of a fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in another language the translation must contain the description, claims, text matter of drawings and abstract; failure to file translation within the required period (including paid extension) results in withdrawal. For PCT regional phase the time limits differ (see PCT section: 33 months for Russian translation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination required to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is granted after substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT regional-phase applications an explicit request for substantive examination must be filed and the examination fee paid within specified deadlines (31 months or within six months of publication of the ISR, whichever is later). Examination request late-filing may be allowed with additional fee and evidence of reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eurasian unitary effect and maintenance per Contracting State
rubrics_metrics.description: A granted Eurasian patent is a single unitary patent valid for all Contracting States together; maintenance is effected by paying annual fees to the Eurasian Patent Office in respect of each Contracting State for which protection is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not possible to obtain a Eurasian patent for only some Contracting States; after grant, the owner indicates which Contracting States the patent will remain valid in by paying the relevant annual fees. Failure to pay for a State causes loss of effect in that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT regional-phase time limits (entry & translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit for entering the Eurasian regional phase: 31 months from the filing/priority date. Time limit for filing Russian translation: 33 months from filing/priority date (extendible by two months upon payment of a fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special form for entering regional phase is available in Russian and preferable. Further PCT particulars: names/address of inventor, appointment of representative for non-residents, and the international search report substitutes the EAPO search report. Examination request deadlines and fee reductions tied to ISR also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-date formal requirements / minimum content for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A Eurasian patent application receives a filing date if at least: a statement that the application is filed as a Eurasian patent application, contact information about the applicant, and a part which on the face of it appears to be a description of the invention are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing elements are identified the Office notifies the applicant and allows four months to supply missing documents; if not supplied the application is regarded as not filed. References to earlier applications in Russian may replace the description for filing date purposes subject to follow-up certified copy and translation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to file first with national office (where required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants from Contracting States requiring first national filing must file Eurasian applications with their National Patent Offices; such filings have same effect as filing directly with the EAPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Eurasian application filed with a National Office must be in four copies compared with three if filed directly with the Eurasian Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant (form and contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for grant must be executed on the prescribed printed form in Russian in triplicate, completed and signed; must contain statement application filed under EAPC, applicant and representative details, title of invention, inventor name/address, and priority claim where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surname(s) and initials of signatory must be mentioned. The request is a mandatory formal part of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants not residing or established in a Contracting State must appoint a Eurasian patent attorney as their representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation requirements also apply when entering regional phase of a PCT application; failure to appoint may result in invitation to comply within a specified time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If representative is a Eurasian patent attorney a power of attorney does not need to be filed except where mandatory; otherwise power of attorney signed by applicant is required (no legalization or notarization required) and generally should be submitted within two months from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general power of attorney valid for all Eurasian applications of same applicant can be used. Inventor must be mentioned unless inventor requests not to be mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description / sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification must disclose the invention in a sufficiently clear and complete manner so as to enable the invention to be implemented by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must contain: title, definition of technical field, definition of background art (preferably citing closest solution), disclosure describing technical problem and technical result, list/brief description of drawings and other material, and information supporting possibility to carry out the invention. For biological material not publicly accessible a deposit with an International Depositary Authority (Budapest Treaty) must be made on or before filing/priority date. Sequence listings should be provided on machine-readable media per prescribed procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirements (structure, clarity, support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define the subject matter for which protection is sought. Claims must be clear and concise and must be fully supported by the specification. Number of claims must be reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim must be one sentence, generally with an introductory (pre-characterizing) part and a characterizing part preceded by words such as 'characterized in that' or 'wherein the improvement comprises'. Claims should not refer to the specification or drawings except if absolutely necessary. Claims may be independent or dependent; dependent claims must specify development or precise features of the independent claim and should be grouped together. Multiple dependency of claims is allowed. Additional claims fees apply for claims exceeding five (and further thresholds). Unity requirement: group of inventions forming single inventive concept defined by common technical features; multiple inventions allowed only if unity satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be as concise as the disclosure allows and should not exceed 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must summarize description, claims and drawings; specify technical field/main field of use and gist of invention mentioning technical result. Abstract must be accompanied by at least one drawing with reference numerals in brackets for each essential feature. Abstract is only for technical information and not for interpreting scope of protection. Where applicable include chemical formula that best characterizes invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be black, indelible, well-defined lines on A4 durable paper; scale and clarity such that details are distinguishable after linear reduction to two-thirds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brackets/circles/inverted commas may not be used with numbers/letters. Numbers and letters in drawings must be at least 3.2 mm high. Drawings may not contain text matter except single words where indispensable. No dimensions in drawings (give dimensions in specification). Reference numerals must correspond between drawings and specification; explanatory material other than drawings must be presented as graphic material (tables, diagrams, photographs only to complement other graphic material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formatting and physical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All parts must be on A4 white, smooth paper; minimum margins (top 2 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 2 cm, bottom 2 cm); each part begins on new sheet; sheets numbered from second sheet; text 1.5 spaced in black type with capital letters at least 2.1 mm high; only one side of sheets used; sheets free from creases and cracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic symbols, Latin/Greek names and formulas may be inserted by hand in India ink or black fountain-pen/ballpoint-pen ink but mix of printed and handwritten matter in same formula not allowed. All parts must allow long-term storage and direct reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: payment, currency, evidence and reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Official fees due to EAPO are fixed in Russian Roubles. A document evidencing payment must be submitted, indicating application title/serial number or patent number and action for which fee is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions: natural persons from certain states pay 50% of prescribed fee; natural persons from Contracting States pay 10%; scientific/educational organizations from Contracting States pay 30%; other entities from Contracting States pay 90%. Reductions apply to fees for filing, appeals, substantive exam, grant, amendments, restoration and assignment. Specific fee amounts and surcharges listed in the fee table (single procedural fee, additional claims fees, examination fee, accelerated processing fees, late-payment surcharges, restoration fees, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of annual maintenance / renewal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: After grant, annual maintenance fees must be paid in respect of each Contracting State for which the patent should remain effective; fees paid before or on the anniversary of the filing date (international filing date for PCT applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount equals aggregate sum of annual fees for maintenance in the Contracting States for the corresponding year; EAPO distributes shares to Contracting States. Grace period of six months for paying annual maintenance fees with 50% surcharge for late payment. Where a patent is granted after the beginning of year for which first fee is payable, amount due includes fees for coming year and preceding years. Non-payment causes loss of effect in that Contracting State. Restoration after unintentional lapse may be available (see restoration rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of missed time limits (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of rights may be available for some missed time limits on request, subject to specific deadlines and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for restoration of the right to a Eurasian application shall be filed not later than twelve months from the date of expiry of the prescribed time limit and not later than two months from removal of cause; no restoration is possible for failure to comply with certain time limits (term for filing opposition; six months term for late payment of annual fees; two months term for late payment of grant fee; term for requesting restoration). Restoration of a Eurasian patent terminated for failure to pay maintenance fee may be requested within three years starting from the date of expiry of the original time limit for payment of the fee not respected. PCT-related restoration procedures (Rule 26bis.3, Rule 49ter) and exceptions are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment requirements and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of a Eurasian patent application and a granted patent can be made only for all Contracting States and must be in writing and registered in the Register of Eurasian Patents to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for registration: assignment deed signed by assignor and assignee; power of attorney signed by assignee; payment of required fee. Neither notarization nor legalization is required. Registered assignment information is published in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences and compulsory licences
rubrics_metrics.description: Licence agreements for a Eurasian patent may be concluded and must be registered according to national law of the Contracting States where the patent has effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National offices inform EAPO quarterly of registered licence agreements and EAPO enters particulars in the Register and Gazette. Compulsory licences may be granted in conformity with the Paris Convention by competent authorities in Contracting States and are effective only in the State where granted; decisions can be contested before national courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge and seizure of application/patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a Eurasian application or patent may be pledged where national legislation provides; EAPO registers the pledging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pledge agreement must be in writing and signed by the parties; EAPO publishes information on registration of the pledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants and entitlement (who may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, successor in title (assignee), joint inventors or their successors irrespective of nationality or domicile may apply for a Eurasian patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more inventors made the same invention independently, right belongs to applicant with earliest filing/priority date. If identical inventions have same filing/priority date, single patent may be granted by agreement between applicants; if no agreement is reached, no Eurasian patent is granted. Employer/employee rights determined by law of State where employee mainly employed or where employer has place of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific treatment for chemical compositions and pharmaceuticals
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical products and pharmaceutical products may be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pharmaceuticals may also be eligible for term extension/SPC in most Contracting States (see national chapters); disclosure and claim drafting guidance (e.g., for second medical use) provided elsewhere in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second medical use / 'use' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Both first and second use may be patentable. If invention is use of a known device/method/substance/product for a previously unknown purpose, claims should identify the known item and indicate that the subject matter is the use for the new purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested claim structure: 'Use of device/method/substance/product X as…/for…/in the manufacture of [the purpose]'. Ensure claims contain features necessary to identify the known item and the new purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment methods and medical procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Patent System allows obtaining patents for methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and methods for medical diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier wording indicated methods for treatment/diagnosis were not designated unpatentable; the manual clarifies that such methods can be patented under the system. Drafting and claim strategy should follow guidelines on claims and second medical use where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological materials and gene sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Microbiological methods, microorganism strains and strains of plant and animal cells may be patented; gene sequences may be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invention involves a microorganism or material not adequately disclosed to enable execution, deposit with an International Depositary Authority under the Budapest Treaty must be made before or on filing/priority date. Sequence listings should be provided on machine-readable media as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant varieties and animal breeds excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant varieties cannot be patented; patents are not granted for animal breeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law and other regimes (e.g., plant variety protection) may interact; consult national chapters for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software-related inventions (nuanced treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual contains apparently differing statements: summary initially states 'computer programs are not patentable' while a later section states 'computer-related inventions (inventions involving the use of a computer program) may be patented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: pure computer programs as such are excluded, but computer-related inventions with technical character or involving a technical contribution may be patentable. Claim drafting should emphasize technical features and practical application to satisfy patentability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business methods exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of economic organization and management (business methods) cannot be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed to purely economic or organizational methods are excluded; embedding such methods in technical implementations may require demonstrating technical effect to seek patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immoral inventions / public order exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions the commercial use of which is to be prevented to protect public order or morality cannot be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject-matter that contravenes public order or morality is excluded; consult national chapters for application and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiconductors / topographies exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Topographies of integrated circuits cannot be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other semiconductor-related inventions (processes, devices) may still be patentable if they meet patentability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty effect of earlier unpublished Eurasian or national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents of earlier Eurasian patent applications form prior art for novelty if subsequently published; earlier PCT international applications designate EAPO count for novelty only if they enter the regional phase; prior rights arising from unpublished national applications may affect later Eurasian applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These earlier applications form prior art only for novelty, not for inventive step determination. The EAPO may not have access to unpublished national applications during examination, but such prior rights can still adversely affect later applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedural points for PCT entering regional phase
rubrics_metrics.description: When designating the Eurasian Patent Office in a PCT application it is valid for all Contracting States. Receiving Office and ISA/IPEA particulars provided: EAPO may act as Receiving Office; ISR by Rospatent or EPO depending on language; timelines for fees, translation, examination and processing explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees: within 31 months a single procedural fee (filing, novelty search, publication) and special claims fee for claims over the fifth must be paid; fee reductions available if ISR prepared by an ISA; average processing time from entry to grant ~2 years. Specific deadlines and fees enumerated in the PCT section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and post-grant procedures (fees and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings exist with associated fees (opposition fee specified in fee table). Publication of amendments after opposition, publication fees, appeal fees and fees for administrative revocation are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition and appeal procedures, fees and timelines are set out; corrected/new specifications amended as result of opposition are published with fees for additional sheets. See fees table for amounts and consult procedural sections for time limits.
